correctness.rationale: Unit Weyl matrices provide an orthogonal operator basis and the orbit projector frame eigenvalues are v times squared Gabor ambiguity. A k-supported window spans only if its support realizes all v-1 nonzero differences, which forces a (v,k,1) difference set. For these supports nonzero displacements yield single products p_x*p_y, and zero displacement is exactly the Fourier transform of the probability weights. Flat difference-set Fourier energy gives the complete three-level spectrum. The pair-product inequality proves the strict optimizer classification and the variance penalty. A concentrated but everywhere positive probability family proves optimality of the rigidity coefficient. All boundaries (k>=3, positivity, singular zero-shift characters) are explicitly treated. The standalone numeric check validates finite instances but is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp global minimax over all smallest-support informative windows, its complete equal-magnitude optimizer class, a weighted rank criterion and the globally sharp variance penalty are compared mathematically with two highly relevant full-text primary papers. Existing universal Gabor diagonalization, Singer difference sets and unweighted constructions are explicitly credited. No inspected theorem provides the full new optimization, although a less-indexed equivalent derivation remains possible.
residual_risks: General Gabor projector spectra are known, so the novelty claim is restricted to the joint extremal classification and quantitative rigidity, not to the spectral diagonalization.
An unindexed historical paper may have performed the same elementary support-product minimax or sharp stability comparison; literature search is not a uniqueness proof.
The nearby multiwindow published finding was compared from a detailed summary only; its full text was not inspected, but the stated domain differs in both window count and objective.

value.rationale: The smallest feasible generator support is an intrinsic information-completeness threshold for single-window complex operator tomography, realized over infinite Singer families. The exact worst-direction spectral conditioning and its complete optimizer class answer a natural sensing-design question rather than an arbitrary support slice. Phase freedom and a best-possible weighted variance penalty give actionable stability information under amplitude imbalance; the result is a natural complete classification, not a modest improved decimal bound.
